Недеља“ — Св. is not a rank and „великомуч.“ is the rank, which `types` already carries; both come off and the bare name is left. **The form is the Serbian vernacular, which is the word for Sunday**, and it is copied as the book prints it and **not transliterated into any form of «Kyriake»**, which is what the other two calendars give and what the slug and display name follow. `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Недеља», so there is no fold — and the same distance that leaves no fold is why `sr-namesweep.mjs` could not find the folder from the name.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru’s name page 2555, «Кириакия (Недела) Никомидийская, …», with the rank words after the last comma left off. The day line gives the name in the genitive only. `fk.mjs` returns no other holder for the folded form.

death.note: doxologia.ro opens «În zilele împăratului Dioclețian, la anul 282», which is the year it gives for her parents' vow, and places her trial before Diocletian, the caesar Maximian at Nicomedia and the governors of Bithynia; the interval is Diocletian's persecution, which the page names but does not date her death within.

attestations.note: The day’s sixth entry, and this folder’s woman: the same menologion day its Romanian, Greek and Serbian rows already keep, the same virgin martyr. Name page 2555 heads her «Кириакия (Недела) Никомидийская, мц.» and lists «День памяти: 7 июля» and no other day — and the bracketed «(Недела)» is exactly the Serbian «Недеља» this folder already stores, the two names the one day of the week, so the identification needs nothing beyond the page. THE READING life4177 WAS NOT OPENED. `dates` UNCHANGED: the line gives «(IV)», the fourth century, which overlaps rather than contradicts the folder’s «under Diocletian», and no interval was widened on a Roman numeral. `types` UNCHANGED — the line grades her «Мц.» where the folder holds `great-martyr, virgin` off the other three calendars, and nothing was removed on the shorter abbreviation. One hymn taken, «Тропарь мученицы Кириакии», whose text addresses her by the other name, «Недело преславная». TWO ENTRIES OF THIS DAY WERE WITHHELD AND ARE NAMED IN THE REPORT: «Прп. Акакия , о котором повествуется в Лествице (VI).» is `acacius-the-obedient`, which already carries a VENERATED russian row on the Julian 29 ноября, and «Прп. Евфросинии, в миру Евдокии , кн. Московской (1407).» is `euphrosyne-of-moscow`, which already carries one on the Julian 17 мая, the day of her tonsure. BRIEF-RUSSIAN §4 forbids a draft on such a folder and BRIEF.md §4 sanctions a second-day note; the author has not ruled between them, so nothing was written for either and their hymns on this page were not copied.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 20.07.2026 (7. јул ст. ст.) — „Св. великомуч. Недеља“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 7 July is the same menologion number this folder’s Romanian and Greek rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. **HOW THIS FOLDER WAS FOUND, AND IT IS THIS RANGE’S FIRST NAMESWEEP FALSE NEGATIVE.** „Недеља“ is the Serbian vernacular — and it is **the word for Sunday**, not a form of the name at all, so no rule over letters could ever bridge it to «Kyriake»: `ndl` against `krk`. `sr-namesweep.mjs` printed one row for this heading, `hope-daughter-of-sophia`, and **did not print the right folder at all**, which is exactly the false negative §7 of this wave’s brief says to watch for. The folder was found off `sr-cand.mjs`’s menologion-number list and then **identified on the scene, not on the name**: the entry opens with two devout old childless people in Anatolia, „Доротеј и Јевсевија“, who begged this child of God by unceasing prayer — and the folder’s own display name is «Kyriake, daughter of Dorotheus and Eusebia». The rest of the entry confirms it: Diocletian and his son-in-law Maximian, the trial at Nicomedia, the commanders. **The alias „Недеља“ → kyriake was added to `.tmp/sr-namesweep.mjs`** and the sweep then prints `kyriake-daughter-of-dorotheus` as its first `!!` row. **A STATED YEAR REFUSED BECAUSE IT WOULD NARROW THE OTHER BOOK’S RANGE.** The folder holds `death` 282 to 305, display «under Diocletian», `traditional`, off doxologia, whose own note says the page «names but does not date her death within» the persecution. This book ends „Чесно пострада и пресели се у вечну радост 289 год. у Никомидији“ — she suffered honourably and passed into eternal joy in the year 289, at Nicomedia. **289 lies inside 282 to 305**, so there is no disagreement to widen; and writing it would replace a recorded interval with a point, which is a date that narrows a source’s range and is refused. `dates` is passed back verbatim, note and all, the year and the city are written into the life, and **the alternative is one edit for the author**: `death` 289 to 289, display «289», basis traditional, with both books’ sentences in the note. WHAT IS NEW. The whole shape of the trial, which the folder had only in outline. That the parents’ accuser was **one of her own rejected suitors**; that the parents were tortured and then banished to the city of **Melitene**, where they ended in torments for Christ; that Diocletian sent her to Maximian, who had her laid on the ground and scourged with ox-sinews; that she was given to a commander Hilarion and, after his death, to Apollonius; that lying in prison all in wounds she was visited and healed by Christ himself, who said to her „Не бој се, Недељо, мука, благодат је моја с тобом“; that grace saved her from the fire and from the beasts, at which many pagans believed in Christ **and all of them were beheaded**; her answer to Apollonius, which answers four torments with four examples out of Scripture and is quoted in the note below rather than in the prose; and the end, that she knelt and prayed God to have mercy on all who should keep her memory and to give her soul rest together with her parents’ souls, **and gave up her soul before the sword came down on her head**. **THE ANSWER TO APOLLONIUS, WHOLE, AND WHY ITS NAMES ARE HERE AND NOT IN THE PROSE.** „Никојим начином не можеш ме одвратити од вере моје. Бациш ли ме у огањ, имам пример Три Отрока; бациш ли ме пред зверове, имам пример Данила; бациш ли ме у море, имам пример Јоне пророка, предаш ли ме мачу, сетићу се Чеснога Претече. За мене је живот за Христа умрети.“ Four of those are folders whose display names are the bare words — `daniel-the-prophet` is «Daniel» and `jonah-the-prophet` is «Jonah** — and `related-floor` reads a prose name whether it is linked or not. **An example quoted in a martyr’s answer is not a relation**, so the names are set down here and the paragraph says «the Three Children», «the prophet in the lions’ den», «the prophet the fish swallowed» and «the Honourable Forerunner» instead. §6’s method applied **before** the test rather than after it, for the first time in this range. `types` UNTOUCHED: `great-martyr` and `virgin` are both there, and „великомуч.“ is the `great-martyr` — **a rank word in the heading that the folder already holds**, so the Cyprian case of 5 July does not recur. Свети is not a rank. No `office`, no `locations`: Anatolia, Melitene and Nicomedia in a narrative are not coordinates, and the folder’s dates read as a twenty-three-year interval which `map-span` would have to answer for. **NO ROWS.** Her parents have no folders: `ls saints | grep -i eusebia` holds **nobody**, and of the thirteen folders whose name reads as Dorotheus or Dorothea none is this man — an identification off a name in another man’s life is not an identification, and the folder’s own display name already carries both parents as words. Diocletian and Maximian are emperors in a life; Hilarion and Apollonius are her persecutors and not saints, whatever folders share those names; Christ is not a folder of this corpus; the pagans who believed and were beheaded are unnamed, and a narrated martyrdom with no name gets no row and no folder. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. **AND THE REFUSAL THIS DAY MAKES TWICE IS OF A YEAR, NOT OF A PERSON.** Three of the four folders of this day hold a `death` whose display is an **interval** — «under Diocletian» — and in each case this book offers a point **inside** it. Writing the point would **narrow a range the other book states**, which is refused outright; and there is nothing to widen, the point falling inside the interval, so there is no disagreement either. In every case `dates` is passed back **verbatim**, note and all, the year is written into the life where the prose can hold it with its own hedge, and **the alternative edit is named here for the author**. This is the same handling as Lampadius’s hedged century on 5 July, reached by a different road: there the book would not assert, here the book asserts something smaller than what is already recorded. **THE DAY REFUSES NO PERSON.** All three entries are persons, all four names the headings enumerate are held, and all four are upgrades — the third such day of this range, after 4 and 5 July.

hymns.text: Mieluşeaua Ta, Iisuse, Chiriachi, strigă cu glas mare: pe Tine, Mirele meu, te iubesc și pe Tine căutându-Te mă chinuiesc și împreună mă răstignesc și împreună mă îngrop cu Botezul Tău; și pătimesc pentru Tine, ca să împărățesc întru Tine; și mor pentru tine, ca să viez pentru Tine; ci, ca o jertfă fără de prihană, primește-mă pe mine ceea ce cu dragoste mă jertfesc Ție. Pentru rugăciunile ei, ca un milostiv, mântuiește sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfintei Mari Mucenițe Chiriachi», Glasul 4

english.text: Your ewe-lamb Kyriake cries out to You, Jesus, with a loud voice: You, my Bridegroom, I love, and seeking You I am in torment; I am crucified with You and buried with You in Your baptism; I suffer for You, that I may reign in You, and I die for You, that I may live in You. Receive me, then, as an unblemished sacrifice, who sacrifice myself to You in love. At her prayers, as the merciful One, save our souls.

hymns.text: Одолением чудесным/ победила еси вражия силы до конца,/ Недело преславная,/ идоложрения бо тьму/ далече Креста честнаго светлостию прогнала еси./ Мученице всехвальная,/ Христу Богу молися/ даровати нам велию милость.

english.text: By a wondrous overcoming thou didst conquer the powers of the enemy utterly, O most glorious Nedelya, for by the brightness of the honourable Cross thou didst drive far off the darkness of idol-worship. O martyr worthy of all praise, pray to Christ God to grant us great mercy.
